summary_of_change:
Newmont's operational reality over the trailing four quarters demonstrates an extraordinary cash-generation machine benefiting from structural strength in precious metals pricing, even as it navigates planned mine sequencing and isolated disruptions. In the latest Q2 2026 release, the company delivered robust revenue of $6.12 billion supported by realized gold prices averaging well above $4,400/oz, driving exceptional quarterly operating cash flows of $2.9 billion and record free cash flow of $2.2 billion. Gross margins have remained exceptionally healthy at 65.9%, underscoring the pricing power and quality of Newmont's premier operating assets like Nevada Gold Mines, Boddington, and Lihir.

Physical production volumes have stepped down temporarily in line with management guidance for an anticipated 2026 production trough, registering 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, 7 million ounces of silver, and 17 thousand tonnes of copper produced in the latest quarter. Temporary headwinds, such as the seismic event at Cadia, were handled swiftly with underground rehabilitation completed and operations returning to normal run-rates.

Management has demonstrated uncompromising capital discipline, utilizing massive cash inflows to fund necessary multi-decade growth projects while aggressively returning surplus capital. Since the last earnings call, Newmont returned $1.9 billion to shareholders, including $1.7 billion in share repurchases under its $6.0 billion authorization, all while maintaining an unblemished net-cash balance sheet with $9.0 billion in cash and $+3.75/share in net cash.

market_pricing_in:
At today's share price of $127.96, Mr. Market is pricing Newmont Corporation with a high degree of skepticism regarding the permanence of its record cash flows, treating current high spot gold realizations as a cyclical peak rather than a sustainable structural baseline. Investors are heavily discounting the company's forward earnings power due to well-publicized operational headwinds, including a trough production year in 2026 (~5.3 million attributable gold ounces), climbing all-in sustaining costs driven by diesel and consumable inflation, and a back-half-weighted capital expenditure schedule.

Yet, this bearish narrative creates a profound disconnect when weighed against Newmont's actual operational footprint, pristine net-cash balance sheet, and disciplined capital allocation. The market is pricing the stock at a modest 15.1x price-to-owner-earnings multiple despite the company generating billions in unencumbered free cash flow and actively retiring shares via an aggressive $6 billion repurchase authorization. Rather than reflecting terminal decay, the current multiple discounts a temporary volume trough while ignoring the immense underlying cash generative capacity of Newmont's tier-1 asset portfolio operating in a robust precious metals price environment.
why_it_might_be_right:
1. Starting Baseline: Starting normalized Owner Earnings are $8.49/share ($8,907.5M total) with net balance sheet cash of $+3.75/share ($+3,930M total liquidity).

2. Forensic Business Headwinds: If skeptic headwinds materialize, persistent operational disruptions—such as seismic events at Cadia and grade transitions at Ahafo South and Peñasquito—will combine with sticky cost inflation in labor, diesel, and reagents to push all-in sustaining costs higher while Ghana sliding-scale royalty taxes bite deeper into margins.

3. Skeptic Unit Contraction: Model a prolonged downside volume contraction where attributable gold production drops further to 4.8 million ounces, and by-product credits soften as base metal prices cool, causing realized monetization yields to contract by 15%.

4. Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation: Fixed mining overhead, mandatory maintenance capex, and sticky direct operating costs fail to contract in tandem with lower volumes, crushing Owner Cash Margins from 34% down to 18%, resulting in a degraded Skeptic Year-3 Owner Earnings of $4.85/share ($5,092.5M total).

5. Downside Risk Valuation Floor: Capitalizing the degraded Skeptic Owner Earnings of $4.85/share at a conservative trough multiple of 9.0x P/OE for a narrow moat asset under severe distress yields $43.65/share, which, when combined with an estimated ending net cash position of $11.75/share after burning cash on unyielding capital commitments, establishes a hard Downside Floor Target of $55.40/share.

what_if_it_keeps_going_that_way:
1. Starting Unit Baseline: Exact starting volume units stand at an annualized run-rate of 5.2 million attributable gold ounces, 28 million ounces of silver, and 68 thousand tonnes of copper produced, with an average realized gold price of $4,414/oz, by-product CAS of $1,043/oz, and AISC of $1,621/oz, underpinning an annualized revenue run-rate of $24,472.0M.

2. 3-Year Unit Volume Extrapolation: Project volume units to recover steadily from the 2026 trough as development assets like Tanami Expansion 2 and Cadia Panel Caves come online, lifting attributable gold production back to 5.7 million ounces by Year 3 while stabilizing co-product output.

3. Projected Year 3 Revenue (Units x Monetization): Multiplying Year 3 volume units by a stabilized long-term monetization yield averaging $4,300/oz realized gold price yields a Projected Year 3 Revenue of $25,850.0M.

4. Cash Cost Structure & Projected Owner Earnings: Deducting normalized cash operating expenses, sustaining capital expenditures of $1,950M, and stock-based compensation of $130M from Year 3 Revenue results in a Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $9,412.5M, representing an Owner Cash Margin of 36.4% and an improved per-share owner earnings of $9.38/share (reflecting a reduced share count of 1,003.02M shares).

5. Explicit 3-Year Balance Sheet & Capital Allocation Bridge: Starting Net Cash of $+3,930M plus Cumulative 3-Year Free Cash Flow of $18,500M, minus Cumulative Share Buybacks of $6,000M and Growth CapEx of $3,500M, equals an Ending Year 3 Net Cash position of $+12,930M ($12.89/share based on 1,003.02M ending shares).

6. Intrinsic Fair Value Target & Expected 3-Year Return: Projecting a Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate of g₃ = 8.6% (falling into the Steady Compounding category), we apply a disciplined 13.5x P/OE exit multiple strictly from the Narrow Moat Matrix. Year 3 Owner Earnings of $9.38/share x 13.5x ($126.63) + Ending Net Cash of $12.89/share yields an Intrinsic Fair Value Target of $139.52 (or $142.64 inclusive of cumulative dividends). This delivers an expected 3-year annualized return (IRR) of 3.69% per annum from today's $127.96 market price.
full_html_content:
What the Market is Pricing In

At today's share price of $127.96, Mr. Market is pricing Newmont Corporation with a high degree of skepticism regarding the permanence of its record cash flows, treating current high spot gold realizations as a cyclical peak rather than a sustainable structural baseline. Investors are heavily discounting the company's forward earnings power due to well-publicized operational headwinds, including a trough production year in 2026 (~5.3 million attributable gold ounces), climbing all-in sustaining costs driven by diesel and consumable inflation, and a back-half-weighted capital expenditure schedule.

Yet, this bearish narrative creates a profound disconnect when weighed against Newmont's actual operational footprint, pristine net-cash balance sheet, and disciplined capital allocation. The market is pricing the stock at a modest 15.1x price-to-owner-earnings multiple despite the company generating billions in unencumbered free cash flow and actively retiring shares via an aggressive $6 billion repurchase authorization. Rather than reflecting terminal decay, the current multiple discounts a temporary volume trough while ignoring the immense underlying cash generative capacity of Newmont's tier-1 asset portfolio operating in a robust precious metals price environment.

Why the Market Might Be Right

1
Starting Baseline
Starting normalized Owner Earnings are $8.49/share ($8,907.5M total) with net balance sheet cash of \(+3.75/share (\)+3,930M total liquidity).
1
Forensic Business Headwinds
If skeptic headwinds materialize, persistent operational disruptions—such as seismic events at Cadia and grade transitions at Ahafo South and Peñasquito—will combine with sticky cost inflation in labor, diesel, and reagents to push all-in sustaining costs higher while Ghana sliding-scale royalty taxes bite deeper into margins.
1
Skeptic Unit Contraction
Model a prolonged downside volume contraction where attributable gold production drops further to 4.8 million ounces, and by-product credits soften as base metal prices cool, causing realized monetization yields to contract by 15%.
1
Reverse Operating Leverage & Cash Degradation
Fixed mining overhead, mandatory maintenance capex, and sticky direct operating costs fail to contract in tandem with lower volumes, crushing Owner Cash Margins from 34% down to 18%, resulting in a degraded Skeptic Year-3 Owner Earnings of $4.85/share ($5,092.5M total).
1
Downside Risk Valuation Floor
Capitalizing the degraded Skeptic Owner Earnings of $4.85/share at a conservative trough multiple of 9.0x P/OE for a narrow moat asset under severe distress yields $43.65/share, which, when combined with an estimated ending net cash position of $11.75/share after burning cash on unyielding capital commitments, establishes a hard Downside Floor Target of $55.40/share.

How Things Are Going Now

Newmont's operational reality over the trailing four quarters demonstrates an extraordinary cash-generation machine benefiting from structural strength in precious metals pricing, even as it navigates planned mine sequencing and isolated disruptions. In the latest Q2 2026 release, the company delivered robust revenue of $6.12 billion supported by realized gold prices averaging well above $4,400/oz, driving exceptional quarterly operating cash flows of $2.9 billion and record free cash flow of $2.2 billion. Gross margins have remained exceptionally healthy at 65.9%, underscoring the pricing power and quality of Newmont's premier operating assets like Nevada Gold Mines, Boddington, and Lihir.

Physical production volumes have stepped down temporarily in line with management guidance for an anticipated 2026 production trough, registering 1.3 million attributable gold ounces, 7 million ounces of silver, and 17 thousand tonnes of copper produced in the latest quarter. Temporary headwinds, such as the seismic event at Cadia, were handled swiftly with underground rehabilitation completed and operations returning to normal run-rates.

Management has demonstrated uncompromising capital discipline, utilizing massive cash inflows to fund necessary multi-decade growth projects while aggressively returning surplus capital. Since the last earnings call, Newmont returned $1.9 billion to shareholders, including $1.7 billion in share repurchases under its $6.0 billion authorization, all while maintaining an unblemished net-cash balance sheet with $9.0 billion in cash and $+3.75/share in net cash.

What If It Keeps Going That Way

Exact starting volume units stand at an annualized run-rate of 5.2 million attributable gold ounces, 28 million ounces of silver, and 68 thousand tonnes of copper produced, with an average realized gold price of $4,414/oz, by-product CAS of $1,043/oz, and AISC of $1,621/oz, underpinning an annualized revenue run-rate of $24,472.0M.

Deducting normalized cash operating expenses, sustaining capital expenditures of $1,950M, and stock-based compensation of $130M from Year 3 Revenue results in a Projected Year 3 Total Owner Earnings of $9,412.5M, representing an Owner Cash Margin of 36.4% and an improved per-share owner earnings of $9.38/share (reflecting a reduced share count of 1,003.02M shares).

Starting Net Cash of \(+3,930M plus Cumulative 3-Year Free Cash Flow of $18,500M, minus Cumulative Share Buybacks of $6,000M and Growth CapEx of $3,500M, equals an Ending Year 3 Net Cash position of\)+12,930M ($12.89/share based on 1,003.02M ending shares).

Projecting a Year 3 Owner Earnings YoY growth rate of g₃ = 8.6% (falling into the Steady Compounding category), we apply a disciplined 13.5x P/OE exit multiple strictly from the Narrow Moat Matrix.
